title: Scoping an Audit
description: Define what will actually be tested, how, and what the audit deliberately does not cover: choosing a sample by user journey rather than page inventory, building a defensible browser/AT test matrix, fitting the plan to the hours actually budgeted, and writing exclusions the client signs off on before testing starts.

title: Evidence That Holds Up
description: Capture evidence for a finding so a developer can reproduce it without you: exact repro steps rather than a vague description, screenshots and recordings that actually prove the bug, verbatim announcement transcripts, the environment details that change whether something reproduces at all, honest documentation of intermittent findings, and an evidence system that survives a three-week audit with two hundred findings in it.

title: Severity and Prioritisation
description: Rate findings so the most harmful get fixed first, and defend the rating: impact, frequency and workaround as the real inputs to severity, why a blocker is defined by whether the task can be finished at all, why conformance level (A/AA/AAA) is not the same axis as severity, grouping many findings under one root cause, and holding a rating under real pushback from a product owner.
